summary: This work proposes SQUID couplers with small Josephson energies ($E_{J,C}/2\pi \lesssim 1$ GHz) for tunable cross-Kerr coupling between superconducting qubits, enabling high-fidelity CZ gates without introducing additional modes or mode hybridization. A scalable miniaturized mergemon processor architecture is presented where all interactions are mediated by junction-based couplers, achieving predicted 100 µm lattice constants and qubit densities up to $10^6$ per 10 cm × 10 cm.
motivation: Standard capacitive linear coupling limits qubit anharmonicity, coherence, and integration density while mode hybridization in tunable couplers causes leakage errors and restricts gate speed. Merged-element transmons reduce dielectric loss but require a coupling scheme that avoids bulky capacitors and hybridization-induced errors.
method: Full circuit quantization and perturbation theory analyze a SQUID coupler circuit mediating two far-detuned transmon qubits. The cross-Kerr ZZ interaction rate scales as $\zeta^{(1)} \propto \Sigma E_{J,C}\cos(\phi_{e,1}/2)(\phi^{zpf})^4$, controllable via external flux $\Phi_{e,1}$ with an idle point at $\Phi_{off} \approx 0.5\Phi_0$. Adiabatic CZ gates use dynamically shaped flux waveforms; robustness against junction asymmetry up to 20%, flux noise, and crosstalk is verified numerically.
result: A 22 ns CZ gate achieves coherent error $3\times10^{-7}$ with minimal 3.4 ns adiabaticity overhead and $\zeta_{on}/2\pi = -26.9$ MHz for experimentally realistic parameters ($E_{J,1}/2\pi = 11.5$ GHz, $E_{J,2}/2\pi = 20.0$ GHz, $E_{J,C}/2\pi = 0.4$ GHz per junction). Coherence-limited infidelity $\approx 1.8\times10^{-5}$ for $T_1 = 1$ ms; next-nearest-neighbor crosstalk remains $\lesssim 60$ kHz and spectator ZZ crosstalk $\lesssim 100$ kHz for realistic stray capacitances.
